# final_history — final closing-record audit

Lower `a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5`: **approve** for records, history and lifecycle correctness; **approve** for independent core fit.

Upper `87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd`: **approve** for records, history and lifecycle correctness; **approve** for independent core fit.

I found no reproducible correctness defect within this records-only review. These verdicts bind only those two immutable revisions. They do not certify later commits, final publication or hosted CI.

## Scope and independence

Inputs were the mechanically composed `lower-closing.txt`, `upper-closing.txt` and `revisions-closing.json`, the two supplied clones' static code/contracts/Git objects, and my own earlier evidence. Captured reports were checked as historical data, not adopted as another reviewer's reasoning. No other closing verdict or outside worker narrative was read. No delegation, repository edits, commits, ref/config changes, or owner-checkout inspection was performed. Top-level queue startup was skipped as a subagent.

The code comparison pins are lower `5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42` and upper `4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41`. Main is `326d8ed5fa4f89eaa1402a54d8377dba5946be12`. I retain my prior bounded code approvals because the runtime and protocol bytes are unchanged, not because an empty records-only test selection passed. My own preceding lower recheck executed 16/16 selected methods and 178/178 subcases on each interpreter; my upper recheck executed 71/71 methods and 620/620 subcases on each, all with zero skips. Their exact prior commands/results remain in `/private/tmp/agentfold-final-history-lower-r2.md` and `/private/tmp/agentfold-final-history-upper-r4.md`; those are not new closing-audit executions.

## Actual checks and counts

| Check executed in this audit | Lower | Upper |
|---|---|---|
| Exact PR merge range, Python 3.14.6 | exit 0; 0 blocking, 5 advisory | exit 0; 0 blocking, 6 advisory |
| Same exact range, Python 3.9.6 | exit 0; 0 blocking, 5 advisory | exit 0; 0 blocking, 6 advisory |
| Code pin to closing pin, push transition and explicit displaced tip | exit 0; 0 blocking, 5 advisory | exit 0; 0 blocking, 6 advisory |
| Exact PR range, deterministic core scope | exit 0; 11 core paths; actual recovery task recognized | exit 0; 10 core paths; actual repair task recognized |
| Git/records audit, both Python versions | 2/2 interpreter runs pass | same 2 runs audit both layers; pass |
| Regression-record/source audit, Python 3.14 | 1/1 map passes | 1/1 map passes |

All 8 selected gate invocations executed and passed; none skipped. The two complete Git/records audit outputs are identical. These are record and admission checks, not new runtime test executions: **0 runtime methods selected or executed in this closing audit**. The prior runtime panel and parent's full suite are deliberately not rerun.

The preserved ordinary-suite limitation is explicit: five intentional skips per suite invocation (three repository-corpus methods, one macOS filename case, one opt-in record-free projection). Verification records separately identify the three corpus executions on both layers/interpreters and the upper opt-in projection executions. They do not present those exclusions or an empty selection as newly executed runtime coverage.

## Preservation and lifecycle evidence

For each layer, all **107/107 tracked entries outside the permitted record surfaces** match its code pin, including **96/96 runtime, test, template, skill, handbook, service, workflow and contract entries**. Modes and Git object IDs match, not merely rendered text. No new executable or protocol file appears. Thus source capture, review successor identity, timing/context/target/revision checks, hooks and trusted receipt grammar retain the previously reviewed bytes.

All **116/116 main conversation files** and **354/354 main task files** remain exact at their original paths on both layers. Lower retains **20/20** original-PR88 commits outside main and **98/98** original-PR88 conversation files. Upper retains those plus **25/25** original-PR89 commits outside main (including inherited lower commits) and **99/99** original-PR89 conversation files. All 3 lower and 5 upper ancestry assertions passed, including current main, their code pins, and upper's final lower dependency.

Relative to the code pins, lower retains **120/120 history entries**, upper **121/121**; both retain **41/41 entries under `memory/decisions/`**. Both preserve **77/77 existing queue entries other than the generated digest**, including **17/17 existing human question files**. Therefore existing answers, waiting/parked states, review bindings and prior lineage remain byte-identical; only the new external-review authorization question is added.

Lower moves 2 tasks, accounting for all **11/11 prior task files**; upper contains 4 moves, accounting for **20/20 prior task files**. There is no dropped old file or duplicate old-status task. Every changed worklog, existing verification and design retains its complete previous bytes as a prefix. Claimant, mode, filed provenance, parent and repository-scope fields are unchanged. Task/plan completion updates are mutable records; verification exists for every task entering review. The old lower task's test-file count changes from 15 to 16 while its original measured output remains intact. The recovery task explicitly lists the new canonical action; no human question is used to put a task in the agent-blocked state.

The new question is `waiting` with a blank human response and exactly `Blocks now: operation:external-recovery-code-review`. It does not block task start, review, completion or Git publication. Full context and resolution evidence both point to the stable memory fact rather than a moving task path. Its excerpt matches that fact exactly, and the fact's action projection exactly copies Action, Why this matters and If you do nothing. The records explicitly preserve the refused execution and missing Claude result; none represents an external verdict as executed.

Upper adds exactly one handover, first created at `87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd`. Its **16/16 entries** exactly match all current unanswered human actions, in the contract's timing-then-queue-path order. Each entry copies all three required values; `Next steps` is `None.`. It retains the v1 projection marker and the unchanged committed-handover integrity gate. Lower adds no handover and modifies none.

## Evidence-record integrity

All **10/10 unique captured report payloads** encode back to their recorded UTF-8 SHA-256: 5/5 lower captures and 10/10 captures present in upper, including the inherited five. My lower and upper captures are also byte-identical to my **2/2 original reports**. I did not reopen other reviewers' original report files; their original-author authenticity is not independently re-established beyond the captured text/digest consistency. Their verdict strings are not inputs to my verdict.

The lower regression map accounts for all **31/31 recovery-added methods**: 29 initial rows plus 2 later portability methods, preserving all **507/507 original PR88 method names** among 538 current methods. Each initial green row records an executed, unskipped pass and an executed assertion-failing control without execution errors. The recorded later 2-method/24-failure control agrees with my own prior evidence. All 29 initial method bodies still match their stated focused code revision.

The upper map covers all **74/74 additions** beyond original PR89, preserving **512/512 original method names** among 586 current methods. All 74 method-source hashes and the recorded test/runtime blob IDs match the closing candidate. Both interpreter summaries agree with their 74 row results and **1,072/1,072 recorded subcases**; all 74 chosen controls contain an actual assertion failure, with no error or skip substituted for failure. These are validated historical result rows, not methods rerun today.

The map's separate identifier and decimal digests match my own prior exhaustive arrays for **1,114,112/1,114,112 code points** on both interpreters. This independently corroborates the preserved Unicode evidence without adopting the coverage reviewer's conclusion.

The publication snapshot names the exact earlier code heads, bases, synthetic candidates and four successful required-check records per layer. Its heads are deliberately not the closing pins. Both verification files explicitly say subsequent record commits are checked and published separately. The records retain this distinction rather than claiming that code-head CI proves a later revision.

## Independent core fit

Both pass agent, provider and unrelated-repository substitution. The completed design receipts describe portable Markdown/Git/source and lifecycle repairs. Closing records add evidence, task status and a bounded human authorization question; they introduce no runtime/provider integration, user-global state or external execution. Naming Claude in a historical refusal and pending authorization is not a core mechanism dependent on that provider. The deterministic gates pass against the changed task inputs and actual task branches. `--require-review` was not invoked; this report is the independent judgment, not a claim that a formal receipt has already been published.

## Reproduction and limits

Environment observed: macOS arm64; Git 2.55.0; `python3` is Python 3.14.6 / Unicode 16.0.0; `/usr/bin/python3` is Python 3.9.6 / Unicode 13.0.0. All commands below use `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. No fixture repository was needed. All written files are under `/private/tmp/final-history-closing-*` plus this requested report.

From `/private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-closing`:

```sh
GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --check --at-transition merge --branch task/2026-08-30-rebuild-the-open-pr-stack --range 326d8ed5fa4f89eaa1402a54d8377dba5946be12...a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5 > /private/tmp/final-history-closing-lower-py314-range.log 2>&1
GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /usr/bin/python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --check --at-transition merge --branch task/2026-08-30-rebuild-the-open-pr-stack --range 326d8ed5fa4f89eaa1402a54d8377dba5946be12...a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5 > /private/tmp/final-history-closing-lower-py39-range.log 2>&1
GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --check --at-transition push --branch task/2026-08-30-rebuild-the-open-pr-stack --range 5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42...a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5 --displaced-tip 5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42 > /private/tmp/final-history-closing-lower-continuity.log 2>&1
GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 automation/check_core_scope.py --range 326d8ed5fa4f89eaa1402a54d8377dba5946be12...a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5 --branch task/2026-08-30-rebuild-the-open-pr-stack > /private/tmp/final-history-closing-lower-core.log 2>&1
```

From `/private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-closing`:

```sh
GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --check --at-transition merge --branch task/2026-08-30-repair-human-question-evidence --range a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5...87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd > /private/tmp/final-history-closing-upper-py314-range.log 2>&1

GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --check --at-transition push --branch task/2026-08-30-repair-human-question-evidence --range 4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41...87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd --displaced-tip 4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41 > /private/tmp/final-history-closing-upper-continuity.log 2>&1
GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 automation/check_core_scope.py --range a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5...87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd --branch task/2026-08-30-repair-human-question-evidence > /private/tmp/final-history-closing-upper-core.log 2>&1
```

The scratch audits address both clones by absolute path and assert HEAD:

```sh
GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /private/tmp/final-history-closing-audit.py > /private/tmp/final-history-closing-audit.log 2>&1
GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /usr/bin/python3 /private/tmp/final-history-closing-audit.py > /private/tmp/final-history-closing-audit-py39.log 2>&1
GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /private/tmp/final-history-closing-regression-audit.py > /private/tmp/final-history-closing-regression-audit.log 2>&1
```

Two initial scratch-audit attempts failed on my harness assumptions (basename rather than full queue path ordering; two historical JSON spellings for skip/subcase counters). I corrected only the scratch scripts to the actual contract/schema and reran them successfully; neither failure was a repository defect. Their outputs remain in `final-history-closing-audit-initial-sort-error.log` and `final-history-closing-regression-audit-initial-schema-error.log`.

Both clones have independent `.git` directories. Index, HEAD, config, refs and clean status match fingerprints taken before substantive gates/audits; final staged and unstaged diffs are empty. The initial upper read-only `git status` preceded those fingerprints, so they do not establish whether that first status refreshed index cache metadata. All subsequent Git-bearing checks disabled optional locks. Evidence is in `final-history-closing-{lower,upper}-before.json` and `final-history-closing-final-preservation.log`.

Parent-owned limits remain: final hosted CI/publication, external execution provenance beyond these immutable records, owner checkout/backup preservation, cleanup and later closing receipts. No live external service was queried or contacted. This review introduces no new human action; the existing authorization item preserves no transmission as its unattended outcome.
